message.abstract: <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title><jats:p>Dynamic control of endothelial cell junctions is essential for vascular homeostasis and angiogenesis. We recently provided genetic evidence that <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">ANGPTL4</jats:styled-content> is a key regulator of vascular integrity both during developmental and in hypoxia‐induced pathological conditions. The purpose of the present study was to decipher the molecular mechanisms through which <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">ANGPTL4</jats:styled-content> regulates vascular integrity. Using surface plasmon resonance and proximity ligation assays, we show that <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">ANGPTL4</jats:styled-content> binds integrin αvβ3. <jats:italic>In vitro</jats:italic> and <jats:italic>in vivo</jats:italic> functional assays with <jats:italic>Angptl4</jats:italic>‐deficient mice demonstrate that <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">ANGPTL4</jats:styled-content>–αvβ3 interaction is necessary to mediate <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">ANGPTL4</jats:styled-content> vasoprotective effects. Mechanistically, <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">ANGPTL4</jats:styled-content>–αvβ3 interaction enhances Src recruitment to integrin αvβ3 and inhibits Src signalling downstream of vascular endothelial growth factor receptor 2 (<jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">VEFGR2</jats:styled-content>), thereby repressing hypoxia‐induced breakdown of <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">VEGFR2–VE</jats:styled-content>‐cadherin and <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">VEGFR2</jats:styled-content>–αvβ3 complexes. We further demonstrate that intravitreal injection of recombinant human <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">ANGPTL4</jats:styled-content> limits vascular permeability and leads to increased adherens junction and tight junction integrity. These findings identify a novel mechanism by which <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">ANGPTL4</jats:styled-content> counteracts hypoxia‐driven vascular permeability through integrin αvβ3 binding, modulation of <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">VEGFR2</jats:styled-content>–Src kinase signalling, and endothelial junction stabilization. We further demonstrate that <jats:italic>Angptl4</jats:italic>‐deficient mice show increased vascular leakage <jats:italic>in vivo</jats:italic> in a model of laser‐induced choroidal neovascularization, indicating that this newly identified <jats:styled-content style="fixed-case">ANGPTL4</jats:styled-content>–αvβ3 axis might be a target for pharmaceutical intervention in pathological conditions. title: <scp>ANGPTL4</scp>–αvβ3 interaction counteracts hypoxia‐induced vascular permeability by modulating Src signalling downstream of vascular endothelial growth factor receptor 2
